title: Maintaining Awareness

inline.s: So how do we cultivate awareness and maintain it at all times and in all places? How do we turn everyday life into practice and take joy in it? The Collected Works of Thich Nhat Hanh says:

You may ask, while washing the dishes, binding books (bookbinding was Thich Nhat Hanh's daily work, and in the book he tells how he turned this work into practice), or working in a factory or an office, how exactly do we cultivate awareness? I think you must find the answer for yourself. As long as you do your best to keep the inner light of awareness bright, you will eventually discover the way that suits you.”

For a Chan master, while washing the dishes, the sacred and the mundane can coexist and blend together without conflict. To be aware of the process of the hands touching the bowls and the water while washing is an experience full of sacredness and wonder, but the key point is to wash continuously and with attention to the present moment.”

There are still many other things to do in life: tending the garden, cooking, doing the laundry, washing the dishes, binding books, and writing. Perhaps these things are not as pleasant as drinking tea or strolling on a hillside, but if we do them with complete awareness, we will find that they are also quite enjoyable. Even washing the dishes after a hearty meal is a delightful thing; every bowl we wash is a miracle.”

Every thought and every action in the light of awareness is sacred. In this luminous realm, the boundary between the sacred and the mundane is dissolved. I admit that I take rather a long time to wash the dishes, but I live in the present moment at all times and my heart is very happy. Washing the dishes is both a means and an end — in other words, washing the dishes is not only to make the bowls and plates clean, but also washing for the sake of washing, so that I maintain awareness in every moment of washing. If I cannot wash the dishes with a joyful heart, but only want to finish them quickly so that I can go and drink tea, then likewise I will not be able to fully enjoy that cup of tea. Although the cup of tea is in my hand, my mind is still dwelling on other things. In this way, the taste of the tea and the joy of savoring it both vanish. My mind is forever suspended in 'the future,' and can never live in 'the present.'”
Remember: what you do is not important; what matters is to be focused and aware in what you are doing.
